cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The blessing of vessels falls on the first day of the month. Every boat in the pound receives the lamp. It takes a morning. The Company has never asked us to stop, and never asked us to hurry.

left.label: The morning is the chapel's
left.outcome: Lamps over every hull. The queue is patient in a way it never is for you.

right.label: Bless them as they pass
right.outcome: "We tend what moves as well as what is still." She adapts.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A Concordance novice, very young, has come to ask the Keeper whether the summit water is the same water as the spring in the chapel. Her teacher told her to ask an engineer. There is none about.

left.label: The same water
left.outcome: She is pleased. It is, as it happens, true.

right.label: Ask Sister Hale
right.outcome: "I did. She said to ask an engineer."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The chapel's roof leaks. Sister Hale has asked me, as landlady, and I have asked the Company, as its tenant is the town's comfort. The Company has asked you. Everyone has asked someone.

left.label: Pay for the roof
left.outcome: Tamm mends it in a day. Hale blesses the ladder.

right.label: The landlady's roof
right.outcome: "Kindly. I shall mend it, and raise the lease."

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The chapel woman feeds our children at her gate. We do not attend her chapel. She has never asked us to. We ask whether the gate thinks that is kindness, or patience.

left.label: Kindness
left.outcome: "Perhaps. We have known patient people who fed us too."

right.label: Ask her yourself
right.outcome: "We do not ask the water. She does not ask us. We are alike, she and we."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Hale's asked the moot to make the Lamp Vigil a town holiday. Half the town would take any holiday. The other half says the chapel's the Company's chapel, founded on Company money.

left.label: Support the holiday
left.outcome: The town takes the day. The chapel is full. Ilse sells a great deal of ale.

right.label: Stay out of it
right.outcome: "Wise. Or cowardly. I'll tell you which later."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: A bargee has died in the pound, of drink, at night. His people are Sorrel and far away. The chapel would bury him at the summit and tend the grave. It costs a plot of Company ground.

left.label: A plot of Company ground
left.outcome: The first grave at the summit that is not a Keeper's.

right.label: Send him down to Sorrel
right.outcome: A cold boat goes west. Hale lights a lamp anyway.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A Concordance elder from the Aldmere chapels has come to inspect the summit chapel's 'founding relics'. Hale has said the undercroft is flooded. It is not, this week. She has asked you to say it is.

left.label: The undercroft is flooded
left.outcome: The elder leaves. Hale does not thank you; she does not need to.

right.label: Show him the undercroft
right.outcome: Hale goes very still. The elder finds only damp and old stone. This week.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: I have found the chapel's original lease among my father's papers. It names a donor. The name is not the Company's. I mention it because the Keeper seems the sort who likes to know things.

left.label: Whose name?
left.outcome: "Marrow. An engineer, I believe. Long dead. Kindly forget I said so."

right.label: Old paper is old paper
right.outcome: "Quite. I shall keep it anyway. I keep everything."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: A Sorrel engineer has asked to test the chapel spring. Its flow, its minerals. He is polite. I have said the spring is not a thing to be tested. He has said everything is. I have come to the gate.

left.label: The spring is the chapel's
left.outcome: He leaves. She holds your hand a moment too long.

right.label: Let him test it
right.outcome: Iron, and the pound's own minerals, exactly. He writes it down. So do you.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The chapel woman asked our old singer to sing at her Vigil. The old singer said the song is not for lamps. We ask whether the gate would hear it, if it were sung there.

left.label: I would
left.outcome: "Then perhaps it will be. Perhaps."

right.label: Songs are the Reach's business
right.outcome: "They are. We wondered."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The chapel poor-line at the gate has doubled. Sorrel families, mostly, off the coal boats. Hale feeds them. The town says it's the Keeper's gate, so it's the Keeper's poor. I say nothing. I'm asking.

left.label: Feed them from the Coffers too
left.outcome: The line is fed. The Book has a column Vosk reads twice.

right.label: The chapel feeds; the gate keeps
right.outcome: "Fair. Cold, but fair."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: A vessel asks the old blessing against the Dry Summit. I have not been asked for it in years. Its words mention 'the river under the hill'. I do not know why. We tend. We do not ask.

left.label: Ask anyway
left.outcome: "Old words. Older than the chapel, I think." She will not say more.

right.label: Say the blessing
right.outcome: The words go over the hull. The bargee, Hullfolk, weeps without sound.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A woman in Concordance grey stands at the gate all day, saying nothing, holding an unlit lamp. Bargees find her unsettling. Hale says she is 'keeping a silence'. Nobody knows for whom.

left.label: Let her keep it
left.outcome: At dusk she lights the lamp and walks away. The pound is a mark lower.

right.label: Ask her to keep it in the chapel
right.outcome: She goes. The bargees are relieved and slightly ashamed.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: Sister Hale has taken in a Sorrel deserter and calls it sanctuary. My building. Company lease. Sorrel Escort Company outside asking. I am not a hard woman, but I am a landlady with a lease to protect.

left.label: Sanctuary holds
left.outcome: Solas withdraws his men without a word. Cole raises the lease.

right.label: Hand him to Solas
right.outcome: Solas takes him gently. Hale does not speak to you for a week.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The Concordance in Aldmere has sent a new hymn for the Vigil. It is about reservoirs. I do not think a hymn should be about reservoirs. But the Company paid for the printing.

left.label: Sing the old hymns
left.outcome: "Thank you." The new hymnals line a damp shelf.

right.label: The Company paid; sing it
right.outcome: A hymn about reservoirs. Quenn, in the back pew, does not sing.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Hale's Vigil is tonight and my inn's the only lit building in town. Every year I close for it. Every year I lose a night. This year I'm asking if the Keeper would stand a round for the town after.

left.label: Stand the round
left.outcome: Vigil, then ale. The chapel and the inn both approve, for once.

right.label: Stay open through the Vigil
right.outcome: The inn is lit. The chapel is fuller anyway. Ilse is not sure how to feel.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The chapel's charter men have put a fence around the spring. A fence. Around water. We have not touched it. We wanted the gate to know we have not touched it, and that we noticed.

left.label: Have the fence taken down
left.outcome: Hale does not object. She never does. She looks tired.

right.label: The spring is the chapel's
right.outcome: "So they say. So the charter says. We have read charters."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: You have asked me three times about the water. Whatever it is, it has fed this town for eighty years. If it is not a gift, it has behaved like one. Do not take that from them.

left.label: I will not take it from them
left.outcome: "Then we understand each other. For now."

right.label: They should know what feeds them
right.outcome: "Should. A hard word. I have never used it."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: Pilgrims from the Sorrel chapels have arrived to see the summit spring and found it fenced, or unfenced, and small. They ask the Keeper whether this is really the source. They have walked a long way.

left.label: This is the source
left.outcome: They kneel. Something in you does not.

right.label: The source is under the hill
right.outcome: They look at the hill. One of them writes it down.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The lamp at the chapel door has burned since the founding, they say. A bargee bumped the post and it has gone out. The town is more upset than I expected. Relight it quietly, or make a rite of it?

left.label: A rite
left.outcome: The whole town attends the relighting. It becomes a new tradition by evening.

right.label: Quietly
right.outcome: "Yes. Some things are better tended than seen."
